assessment: The incumbent provides embedded-caption previews and retained history, and succeeds within 15 minutes in 20/30 sessions, below the required 27/30. Its strongest supplied limiting observation is H1-O7: nine single-correction sessions succeeded in five to 11 minutes without version uncertainty. Thus full rendering can support usable previews in a bounded workflow; universal replacement is not established. Completion inversions and unexpected source versions suggest coordination or identification problems, but do not establish their cause. The 49-hour week does not establish festival capacity.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: capture an immutable video-and-caption revision tuple at request time, render exactly those retained sources, and display that same tuple on the completed preview and download entry. This could prevent source drift and make intended previews identifiable despite completion order.
openings.delta: Adds explicit source identity across request, execution and selection while retaining the incumbent render and history workflow.
openings.prediction: With interleaved video and caption edits and deliberately reversed completion order, each artifact matches its recorded tuple and editors select their intended tuple.
openings.probe: Use fabricated footage in private staging; submit overlapping revisions, verify output source hashes and caption wording, and have the two editors identify previews. Check continued access to the last delivered wording. Measure implementation effort and processing overhead before adoption.
assumptions: Existing storage can retain immutable source revisions.
The change fits four engineer-days, one editor-day and the 80-hour allowance; unverified.

openings.claim: Do slow sessions primarily lose time before the intended artifact becomes available, or after availability while identifying and reviewing it?
openings.delta: Distinguishes render scheduling remedies from preview identification remedies.
openings.prediction: A waiting-dominant explanation predicts availability near or beyond 15 minutes; an identification-dominant explanation predicts earlier availability followed by prolonged selection or review.
openings.probe: Align timestamped render events with intended source tuples and timed editor demonstrations; partition final-edit-to-correct-preview time at artifact availability, recording selection and viewing separately.
assumptions: A short private-staging demonstration fits the available editor-day.
Demonstrations can discriminate mechanisms but cannot establish the 30-session success measure.
